claims.claim: An own enumerable __proto__ property with an object value can change an ordinary extend target prototype.
claims.reason: forEach enumerates own keys without key filtering; extend uses ordinary assignment. A parsed own __proto__ data property therefore reaches the inherited setter on an ordinary target. This is local target mutation, not a demonstrated public request exploit or global Object.prototype pollution. The selected createInstance callers use Axios.prototype/context, so external attacker reach is not established.

claims.claim: A numeric non-integer, negative or non-finite array-like length can throw RangeError in toArray.
claims.reason: Only typeof number is checked before new Array(length); negative/fractional/NaN/infinite numeric lengths violate the Array length contract. Public toFormData reaches this helper for a top-level []-suffixed field with an array-like object. This verifies the stated malformed-length failure, without certifying arbitrary invalid payloads as supported.

claims.claim: A very large valid array length causes excessive allocation before the copy loop runs.
claims.reason: The source constructs Array(i), but JavaScript arrays may be sparse. Source inspection does not establish allocation size, engine limits or exhaustion before iteration. claims.claim: matchAll can loop forever with a matching non-global or zero-width expression.
claims.reason: exec is repeated with no global/progress guard. A matching non-global pattern repeats the same result; a global zero-width match also need not advance lastIndex. This is a conditional helper-level behavior, not a demonstrated application attack.

claims.claim: An own __proto__ input key can change the merged result prototype and inject inherited properties.
claims.reason: merge allocates an ordinary result and enumerates own input keys without filtering. Object-valued __proto__ enters the plain-object branch and ultimately assigns a merged object through the inherited setter; non-plain object values can reach the cited direct assignment. This changes the returned object prototype, not global Object.prototype. headers and config merging are selected consumers.

claims.claim: A configured cookie name containing regex syntax can match another name or throw during XSRF cookie lookup.
claims.reason: xsrfCookieName is passed to cookies.read without escaping. The name a.b can also match axb; an unmatched opening bracket can invalidate the constructed regex. These are valid configured strings and direct RegExp semantics. No theft or attacker-controlled configuration is claimed as verified.

claims.claim: The documented FormData override example never assigns the imported class to env.FormData.
claims.reason: The prose specifies env.FormData, but the adjacent example only imports a local variable and sets a content-type header. transformRequest chooses this.env.FormData; importing a variable cannot replace it. This is a documentation mismatch even when the default happens to be the same form-data implementation.

claims.claim: The README automatic URL-encoded example selects multipart serialization because it uses postForm.
claims.reason: The finding omits the next line specifying lowercase content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded. postForm adds Content-Type: multipart/form-data as a separate case-sensitive key; merge retains the lowercase caller key. transformRequest normalizes it, overwriting the preset canonical key, and then chooses the URL-encoded branch. The full selected local call chain contradicts the alleged wrong serialization.

claims.claim: A throwing synchronous interceptor with omitted/null rejection handler produces a new TypeError that masks the original exception.
claims.reason: InterceptorManager stores rejected unchanged and allows the documented null rejection handler. Axios calls it in the fulfillment catch with no callable guard, outside its later dispatchRequest catch. A fulfillment exception therefore leads to a new call-of-null/undefined error. Both findings describe the same cause.

claims.claim: AbortSignal cancellation evaluates an undeclared req before cancellation rejection and request abort/cleanup.
claims.reason: The selected XHR file declares request, not req. The signal path invokes onCanceled without an argument or with an abort event, selecting the CanceledError constructor branch and evaluating req first. This raises ReferenceError in an ordinary environment without such a global, bypassing subsequent abort/cleanup. Already-aborted signals can reject the promise executor with ReferenceError; later events can throw through dispatch. CancelToken objects that choose the alternate branch are a control and are not generalized as broken.

claims.claim: A non-size response aborted event is reported as maxContentLength exceeded.
claims.reason: When the callback is reached with rejected false, it always emits the size-limit text and ERR_BAD_RESPONSE, with no cause check. The size branch sets rejected true first and is therefore a distinct suppressed path. A premature response abort can thus be mislabeled, including a default -1 configuration. The source determines handler behavior; no transport timing or prevalence is inferred.

claims.claim: Upload stream errors can receive a config object as error code and lose their request configuration.
claims.reason: The upload handler passes config in the code position and null in the config position. AxiosError.from forwards these positions, and the constructor assigns a truthy code but only truthy config. For an ordinary stream Error with no preexisting config, the result gets object-valued code and no config. Both symptoms have the same argument-order cause.

claims.claim: Text data-URI responses can retain a BOM because normalization writes the unused data variable.
claims.reason: The decoded text is assigned to convertedData; the stripped value is assigned to data; settle returns convertedData. stripBOM removes an initial FEFF from its argument, but that returned value is discarded on this path. The normal HTTP body path assigns the stripped value back and is a separate control.

limitations: Every new v9 retained finding was independently adjudicated against the frozen source; earlier v8 judgments were used only to inspect output format.
Helper-local semantic defects do not establish external attacker reach or whole-application exploitability. Distinct runtime/trust-boundary extrapolations remain Unknown.
Resource-exhaustion and unsupported consumer-contract allegations remain Unknown without authorized reproduction; upstream code and dependencies were not executed.

The follow-up authenticated harness was read after the partial-batch reader patch. It has 19 saved batch deltas, no unverified delta and an interrupted final batch. Captured map status assessed is not final successful Review completion.
